source.title: Memory-efficient training with streaming dimensionality reduction
source.authors: Si-Yuan Huang; B. Hoskins; M. Daniels; M. Stiles; G. Adam

record.tranche_reason: Tests dropout's effect on classifier accuracy, a condition named in V6, using a 50% dropout setting in AlexNet.
record.gate_note: The paper evaluates streaming batch PCA and dropout against minibatch gradient descent on natural-label image datasets. It does not test random-label memorization, width beyond interpolation, architecture comparisons, optimizer generalization, batch-size effects on the generalization gap, sharpness measures, or removal of memorized examples. Results cited from other work are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The study directly compares held-out classification accuracy with and without 50% dropout in AlexNet fully connected layers, testing V6 with the same basic intervention and measure.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately captures one dropout discussion but overstates the CIFAR-10 improvement and omits the paper's central conclusion. The authors conclude that streaming low-rank gradient updates can reduce theoretical memory and computational requirements while approaching MBGD accuracy. Dropout substantially improves MBGD accuracy on CIFAR-100 and ImageNet, improves it only slightly on CIFAR-10, and has effects that depend on rank when combined with SBPCA. They suggest their dropout integration may be suboptimal.
record.recipe_differences: Evaluates dropout as a comparison within a study of streaming low-rank gradient updates; dropout is applied at 50% in AlexNet fully connected layers. The study does not reproduce the original dropout study's range of regimes.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset and training method change the reported dropout outcome: MBGD improves on CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100, whereas the combined SBPCA methods do not show an equivalent increase; CIFAR-10 is also described as showing almost no change for the smallest network.
record.problems: No dropout-strength sweep is reported. The CIFAR-10 dropout effect is described inconsistently: the smallest network is said to show almost no change, while MBGD performance is also said to increase dramatically. The text does not give numerical values for the MBGD dropout comparison.
record.rows_left_out: The paper reports many SBPCA and SBPCAV accuracy results and rank-dependent comparisons, but these do not directly test a version's named claim except for dropout comparisons captured in R1–R2. Results about the low-rank gradient method's memory use, convergence, and gradient tracking are outside the listed versions.

untested.parts: Random-label memorization and the comparison of natural-label versus random-label held-out accuracy.
Network width beyond the width needed for zero training error; gradient approximation rank is not network width.
Convolutional versus fully connected architectures and learned local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD and the effects of tuning.
Controlled batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and adapted training recipes.
Very small training sets, dropout-strength sweeps and excessive-dropout underfitting, standalone fully connected classifiers, and removing dropout together with weight decay under data augmentation.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its ranking of generalization gaps relative to other measures.
Removing memorized examples versus random examples and retraining.

missing.what: ImageNet MBGD dropout comparison: accuracy 0.4613 without dropout versus 0.5437 with dropout.

Within-SBPCA dropout comparisons on CIFAR-10: ranks 1, 3 and 10 have no-dropout/dropout accuracies 0.7292/0.7386, 0.7542/0.7517 and 0.7710/0.7709. These intervention comparisons bear on V6 beyond the method-performance comparisons described in rows_left_out.

Within-SBPCA dropout comparisons on CIFAR-100: ranks 1, 3, 10, 30 and 100 have no-dropout/dropout accuracies 0.4033/0.3191, 0.4411/0.3993, 0.4522/0.4452, 0.4462/0.4872 and 0.4388/0.5179. These show rank-dependent dropout effects beyond the method comparisons described in rows_left_out.

record.verdict_notes: This study is not an original source for V6. Fig. 10(a) contains readable paired accuracy columns despite inconsistencies in the surrounding prose and caption. No uncertainty is supplied for these paired accuracy values; Fig. 6's error bars concern convergence measurements.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and held-out performance on natural versus random labels.
Width sweeps past the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected comparisons and learned local connectivity.
Large versus small batch generalization under fixed epoch budgets and adapted recipes.
The paper tests 50% dropout only in AlexNet fully connected layers; it does not test very small training sets or a range of dropout strengths.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and comparisons with norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing memorized training examples and retraining.
